chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from al-Husayn, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, and al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The greater pilgrimage is the Day of Adha.

key_terms.يَوْمُ الْأَضْحَى: The Day of Adha (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of the greater pilgrimage (Hajj al-Akbar) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly identifies the Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah) as the 'Greater Pilgrimage' (al-Hajj al-Akbar), a term often used in Shia jurisprudence to denote the culmination of the Hajj rites or the specific day of standing at Arafat and sacrifice. This definition highlights the theological and ritual significance of this day as the peak of the pilgrimage season, distinguishing it from the general concept of Hajj or the lesser pilgrimage (Umrah). The chain of transmission through prominent companions like Abu Basir and Nadr underscores the reliability of this specific jurisprudential classification within the Imami tradition.

en.basel-kadem: 4.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari, from Ibrahim bin Mahziyar, from his brother, Ali, from Hussain, from Hammad bin Isa, from Shu’ayb, from Abu Baseer, and Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
The greater pilgrimage is the Day of Adha.
